d: Victorian and early twentieth-century foundational journeys to the Moon and Mars by Ray Bradbury, H. G. Wells, and Jules Verne.

mars.x: Poetic canals, dying seas, and telepathic crystal cities in Ray Bradbury’s Martian Chronicles, and the desiccated red home of the ruthless tripod-launching invaders in H. G. Wells’ War of the Worlds.
mars.a: bradbury canal crystal tripods cylinder heatray spender

moon.x: Underground caverns of the insectoid Selenites and the Grand Lunar in H. G. Wells’ First Men in the Moon, and the circumlunar trajectory of the Gun Club’s hollow artillery projectile in Jules Verne’s From the Earth to the Moon.
moon.w: The First Men in the Moon
moon.a: selenite cavorite bedford cavor columbiad gunclub verne barbicane

b.s: The earliest masterpieces of space exploration: Jules Verne’s space-cannon Columbiad, H. G. Wells’ Selenite moon and invading Martian cylinders, and Ray Bradbury’s haunting Martian crystal cities.
b.a: Ray Bradbury, H. G. Wells, Jules Verne
b.r: From the Earth to the Moon (1865), The War of the Worlds (1898), and The Martian Chronicles (1950)
